context: Linked scatterplot matrix (SPLOM) data visualization with KDE density on the diagonal, showing 4-dimensional iris-like species data with brushing interaction
first_impression: The color palette and typographic choices show genuine design intent, but the visualization is compromised by empty cells throughout the upper-left region and data visibly overflowing the grid boundary at the top-right.
what_works: Tol colorblind-safe palette (#4477AA / #EE6677 / #228833) with subtle darker-stroke on circles adds polish above generic defaults; typographic hierarchy is real — monospace tick labels recede clearly below bolder column labels, and the subtitle sits unmistakably secondary to the title.
what_doesnt: Most off-diagonal cells in the Sepal Length and Sepal Width rows render completely blank, a fundamental data-visibility failure that floors the 'does it work' check; scatter points visibly overflow the top-right grid boundary, confirming clipping or coordinate mapping bugs that make the visualization untrustworthy as a data tool.
